bullets.title: Why Is Joe Rogan So Popular?
bullets.creator: Devin Gordon
bullets.note:
(_Atlantic_) by Devin Gordon ([@DevinGordonX](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/0pfwh9hwr9polv/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9EZXZpbkdvcmRvblg=)). This is one of the best explorations of Joe that I’ve come across. Devin captures the zeitgeist—with real insight into Joe and his format—better than anyone I’ve seen to date. Here is one of many sections that struck me, slightly edited for length:  

\[One journalist wrote,\] “If traditional media were pissed about anything relevant to the Musk-Rogan interview, it was the extent to which Rogan got played.”

Played! Imagine writing that about one of the most discussed and downloaded podcasts of 2018. Rogan, the one who handed Elon Musk a spliff, on camera, and got him to smoke it, thus earning national headlines for himself and millions of listens for his advertisers, got played. In order to reach such a conclusion, you have to begin with the presumption that interviews must always be a form of combat, with winners and losers….

The hard truth for some of Rogan’s critics in the media is that he is much better at captivating audiences than most of us, because he has the patience and the generosity to let his interviews be an experience rather than an inquisition. And, go figure, his approach has the virtue of putting his subjects at ease and letting the conversation go to poignant places, like the moment when Musk reflected on what it was like to be Elon Musk as a child—his brain a set of bagpipes that blared all day and all night. He assumed he would wind up in a mental institution. “It may sound great if it’s turned on,” he said in his blunt mechanical way, “but what if it doesn’t turn off?”

bullets.section: Near-magical lotion bar that I’m using —
bullets.title: climbOn Lotion Bar
bullets.note: This was introduced to me by Rodney of [Specialized Bicycles](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/e3sph7hwoldprg/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3BlY2lhbGl6ZWQuY29tL3VzL2Vu) on [the Hayduke bike trail](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/ogakhqhld60kqm/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cub3V0c2lkZW9ubGluZS5jb20vMjE5MzM5MS9oYXlkdWtlLW9wdGlvbg==), which we rode from Grand Junction, Colorado, to Moab, Utah. There are a few things I should share as background. First, this was my first real mountain-biking trip of more than five miles, and it was also my first time using clip-in shoes (not smart). Second, my dear friend [Kelly Starrett](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/pqbeh9h5o2p3qn/aHR0cHM6Ly90aGVyZWFkeXN0YXRlLmNvbS90aW0v) told me in advance, “Don’t worry!” (I was worried.) “Have you ever ridden a beach cruiser on the Venice boardwalk? It’ll be like that. Flat fire roads. Super chill.” (Not true.) So—surprise, surprise—I got my ass kicked every which way from Sunday. Rodney repeatedly saved me, and this lotion bar was one tool in his arsenal. Though initially designed for rock climbers, climbOn repeatedly rescued my ankles, feet, and hands, even when I thought my trip was over.

bullets.title: Lynn Margulis
bullets.note: From Wikipedia: She was “an American evolutionary theorist and biologist, science author, educator, and popularizer, and was the primary modern proponent for the significance of symbiosis in evolution. Historian Jan Sapp has said that ‘Lynn Margulis’s name is as synonymous with symbiosis as Charles Darwin’s is with evolution.’” Next up for me is [her debate with Richard Dawkins at Oxford](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/qxu8h7h2p4l7kx/aHR0cDovL3d3dy52b2ljZXNmcm9tb3hmb3JkLm9yZy9ob21hZ2UtdG8tZGFyd2luLXBhcnQtMS1iZWxsLWJyYXNpZXItZGF3a2lucy1ub2JsZS10YWxrcy8=) from 2009 ([Part 1](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/gxinh5howl0dqv/aHR0cDovL3d3dy52b2ljZXNmcm9tb3hmb3JkLm9yZy9ob21hZ2UtdG8tZGFyd2luLXBhcnQtMS1iZWxsLWJyYXNpZXItZGF3a2lucy1ub2JsZS10YWxrcy8=), [Part 2](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/nlfohvh50xl8l8/aHR0cDovL3d3dy52b2ljZXNmcm9tb3hmb3JkLm9yZy9ob21hZ2UtdG8tZGFyd2luLXBhcnQtMi1zeW1iaW9nZW5lc2lzLWZpbG0tYW5kLWRpc2N1c3Npb24v), [Part 3](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/d0u95nv33i0h8ww5zf5/w7t2hghv6kl5lk/aHR0cDovL3d3dy52b2ljZXNmcm9tb3hmb3JkLm9yZy9ob21hZ2UtdG8tZGFyd2luLXBhcnQtMy1nZW5lcmFsLWRpc2N1c3Npb24v)). She was incredibly controversial, and I don’t agree with all of her views, but I do find this type of debate useful in stretching one’s mind.
